title: Resize a Note from any edge or corner
lede: Resize adds no engine code. It is 8 new Drag kinds, one per Resize handle, plugged into the engine from #4. Each one is a pure function from the press rect and the delta to a rect. The Preview now writes `width`/`height` next to the `translate`, and the `resize` action saves the same rect the Preview showed.

files.question: Which part of a Note starts a resize?
files.summary: 8 invisible hit zones. A press on one stops propagation and reports its handle.
files.owns: The handle elements, their cursors, and the `se` tick (in the CSS module).
files.tested: Browser test of every cursor and the single tick.

files.question: Which Drag does a press start?
files.summary: A press on the body starts `moveKind`. A press on a handle starts `resizeKinds[handle]`. Both Raise first.
files.owns: Choosing the Drag kind at press time.
files.tested: Browser tests with real mouse input.

files.question: Which Drag kind does each handle start?
files.summary: `resizeKinds`: one kind per handle, built once. Its Preview and its commit both call `resizeRect`.
files.owns: Turning a rect into a `resize` action.
files.never: Does the edge maths, listens, or touches the DOM.
files.tested: A Node test that the commit equals the Preview.

files.question: What rect does a resize produce?
files.summary: `resizeRect` moves only the named edges, clamped to the minimum Note size and the Board, next to `clampToBoard` for moves.
files.owns: Every rule that keeps a rect legal on the Board.
files.tested: Named examples and fast-check properties in Node.

files.question: How is a resize drawn?
files.tested: Browser tests. Not in the coverage gate.

files.question: When does each thing happen?
files.summary: Unchanged from #4. It runs a resize exactly like a move.

files.question: How does `resize` change the Notes?
files.summary: Commits the rect through `toCommittedRect`. If nothing changed it returns the same state.

scenarios.name: Drag the nw corner and release

steps.title: pointerdown on the nw handle
steps.explain: The handle sits inside the Note, so without `stopPropagation` the Note's own `onPointerDown` would also run and start a move. The controller keeps only one session, so the second `start` would win. `pressHandle` then does what `press` does, Raise and then `start`, with a different kind. `resizeKinds` is built once at import, so the kind passed to `start` is the same object on every press.

steps.title: pointermove past the Dead zone
steps.explain: The controller is the one from #4 and calls `preview` the same way. The kind passes its handle to `resizeRect` as the edges to move. For `nw` both the `n` and `w` branches run. Each moves its edge and recomputes the size from the opposite edge (`right`, `bottom`), so the bottom-right stays fixed. The clamp's upper bound is `right - MIN_NOTE_SIZE.width`, so shrinking stops at 140 px without moving the right edge. The delta is rounded first, so the Preview is already in whole pixels.

steps.title: The Preview is written
steps.explain: The `translate` moves the top-left, and `width`/`height` change the box, so the text reflows instead of stretching as it would under `scale`. The browser test checks that `transform` never contains `scale`. A move goes through the same code and writes the size it already had.

steps.title: pointerup
steps.explain: `commit` calls the same `resizeRect` with the same delta, so the saved rect is the last Preview. The browser test checks that the box after release equals the box during the Drag. `end` resets the Preview to `base` before dispatching, then `resize` commits the rect. `toCommittedRect` changes nothing here because the rect is already legal, but it keeps the reducer safe on its own.

run.to: return withNote(state, { ...note, x, y, width, height });

steps.title: The se corner dragged far inward
steps.explain: `e` and `s` clamp from below at `MIN_NOTE_SIZE`, so the Note stops at 140×100 and its top-left stays put. The browser test drags 250×150 px inward and checks the one `resize` action, the store and the rendered box.

run.to: width = clamp(from.width + dx, MIN_NOTE_SIZE.width, BOARD_SIZE.width - x);

steps.title: Release inside the Dead zone, or back where it started
steps.explain: Inside the Dead zone the controller dispatches nothing, as in #4. Past it, a release at the starting size still dispatches `resize`, and the reducer returns the **same** state, so no Note re-renders. When a Note does change, `withNote` keeps the other Notes by reference. The browser test checks that resizing *b* re-renders only *b*.

run.from: if (x === note.x && y === note.y && width === note.width

steps.title: end(false) resets to base
steps.explain: A reset writes `base`, the rect React rendered at press. `transform` is cleared and `width`/`height` go back to the rendered values. The inline size stays set afterwards, but it equals React's own `style` value, so nothing changes on screen. No browser test covers Escape during a resize. The controller tests from #4 cover the cancel path, which doesn't depend on the kind.

run.from: const { x, y, width, height } = rect ?? base;

notes.title: A resize clamps each edge in `resizeRect`, not with `clampToBoard`
notes.detail: `clampToBoard` keeps the size and moves the Note to fit. That is right for a move and wrong for a resize, where the opposite edge must stay put. So `resizeRect` clamps each moving edge itself, and the reducer's `clampToBoard` never changes a rect that came from a Drag. Both rules sit in `geometry.ts`, so the Board limits are in one file. `geometry.ts` names edges with its own `Edges` type, so it imports nothing from `drag/`.

notes.title: `writePreview` leaves inline width/height set after a reset
notes.detail: They equal what React rendered, and React overwrites them when the size changes. If something else ever set the size outside React's `style`, this would hide it.

notes.title: No Trash zone yet
notes.detail: The issue says a resize never reports being over the Trash zone. The Trash zone isn't in `io` yet (#6), so for now nothing reports it. #6 must keep resize kinds out of it.
